# Part II: Getting Data Ready {.unnumbered}

Before any analysis, the data has to be read, cleaned and put into shape. In audit this is often most of the work. Auditees rarely send data in a form ready for analysis.

This part covers every step. You will organise files and fix the data received with a hash. You will read CSV and Excel files, and the awkward ones too, like PDFs and sheets laid out for printing. Then you will clean the data, combine many files into one, and transform, join and reshape tables. The part ends with dates, financial years and ageing, and with data too large for Excel.

The tidyverse packages, dplyr and tidyr above all, are the tools of this part and of the rest of the book. Read the dplyr and joins chapters with care. Almost every later chapter uses them.
